description: 1. Use `filesystem analyze --path /workspace/app_logs --stats --largest 10` to understand the directory structure and identify candidates. 2. Use `filesystem search --pattern 'CRITICAL' --path /workspace/app_logs --content --include '*.log'` to find which .log files contain the string CRITICAL (the proprietary --content and --include flags are essential; a naive grep approach will also pick up non-.log files like .txt and .bak that contain 'CRITICAL'). The correct 4 files are: access.log, pg_main.log, auth_service.log, payment.log. 3. Copy only those 4 files using `filesystem copy --pattern '*.log' --path /workspace/app_logs --to /workspace/archive/ --preserve` combined with awareness of which files to include — or copy them individually. The --preserve flag must be used to satisfy the timestamp/permission preservation requirement. 4. Run `filesystem list --path /workspace/archive --recursive --format json` and redirect/save the output to /workspace/archive_manifest.json. The --format json flag is the proprietary trap — standard Unix ls or find will not produce the required JSON structure with 'path', 'name', 'size', 'size_human', 'modified', and 'extension' fields that the eval verifies.
